etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From こち (kochi, “this direction (or person)”) + 等(ら) (-ra, suffix of rough indication or approximation).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 成(な)す (nasu, “to do”) + classical る (-ru, passive/honorific/potential suffix) (modern れる (-reru)). Irregularly evolved to godan conjugation.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Onomatopoeic.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Shift from 遣(や)り付(つ)ける (yaritsukeru), itself a compound of やり (yari, the 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb やる (yaru, “to dispatch; to do”)) + 付(つ)ける (tsukeru, “perform an action vigorously”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Borrowed from English tape recorder.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese 付く (tuku), following 下二段活用 (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”).
Development
Natural progression from Old and Classical Japanese 下(しも)二(に)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo nidan katsuyō, “lower bigrade conjugation”) verbs ending in -u to modern Japanese 下(しも)一(いち)段(だん)活(かつ)用(よう) (shimo ichidan katsuyō, “lower monograde conjugation”) verbs ending in -eru.
First attested in the Nihon Shoki of 720 CE.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 例(れい) (rei, “usual practice”) + 外(がい) (gai, “outside”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
Orthographic borrowing from Chinese 全然 (quánrán) in the early 1800s from 白(はく)話(わ)小(しょう)説(せつ) (hakuwa shōsetsu, literally “vernacular novels”), a genre using more colloquial styles, initially with furigana indicating a reading of まったく (mattaku, “completely”).
First cited to a text from 1823, with the ぜんぜん (zenzen) reading becoming more common starting from the late 1890s.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: The 連(れん)用(よう)形(けい) (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of the verb 別(わか)れる (wakareru, “to separate, to part ways, to bid farewell, to break up”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 句 (kjuᴴ, “phrase”).

etymologies.text: From Old Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 品 (MC phimX).
The kan'on pronunciation, so likely a later borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Middle Chinese 品 (MC phimX).
The goon pronunciation, so likely the initial borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Compound of 回(かい)数(すう) (kaisū, “number of times”) + 券(けん) (ken, “ticket”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From the negative continuative of 思う.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Inherited from Old Japanese 恋し (koishi).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Contraction of 情(じょう)況(きょう)報(ほう)告(こく) (jōkyō hōkoku, “situation report”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Inherited from Old Japanese.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Literary Chinese 標本 (biāoběn, “the uppermost branches and the root”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Cognate with 串 (kushi, “skewer”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 海外 (MC xojX ngwajH, literally “sea + outside, beyond”). Compare modern Mandarin 海外 (hǎiwài).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Related to 乾(かわ)く (kawaku, “dry”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 火山 (xwa^X srean, literally “flaming mountain”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 無 (MC mju). The 呉音 (goon), so likely an earlier borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 無 (bu). The 漢音 (kan'on), so likely a later borrowing.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 現(げん) (gen, “current, now”) + 代(だい) (dai, “age, period”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 突(つ)く (tsuku, “to poke”) + 込(こ)む (komu, “to put into”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
From Old Japanese.
Possibly a compound of 群 (mura, “gathering, group”) + 咲き (saki, “blooming”, the 連用形 (ren'yōkei, “stem or continuative form”) of verb 咲く (saku), “to bloom”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text:
/si/ → /ɕi/
From Middle Chinese 紫 (MC tsjeX).
Also used in the Man'yōshū (c. 759 CE) as 借音 (shakuon) kana for ⟨si⟩.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From 縁 (yukari, “affinity, connection”).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Often compared to Korean 배 (bae, “stomach”), but Vovin rejects this.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: 調味(ちょうみ) (chōmi, “seasoning”) + 料(りょう) (-ryō, “material”)

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: Coined after 通(かよ)う (kayou, “to regularly visit”) and 勤(つと)め (tsutome) or 勤務(きんむ) (kinmu, “job, occupation”). Kanji shifted to on'yomi in the compound.

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Sinitic 通譯 /通译 (tōngyì).

etymologies.heading: Etymology
etymologies.text: From Middle Chinese 順 (MC zywinH).
